item.text:
**1B.2 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Bottom line:** the 2024 record I found is mostly **non-escalatory on doctrine**, but not strongly reassuring on rhetoric. The clearest support for “responsible” nuclear language is regime-level denial of nuclear-weapons intent and repetition of the long-standing fatwa line. The clearest contrary evidence is that senior IRGC and advisory figures close to Khamenei used explicit conditional-threat language about changing doctrine if Iran were threatened.

**Supported claims**

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Iran says nuclear weapons have no place in its nuclear doctrine` | Reuters | 2024-04-22 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/iran-says-nuclear-weapons-no-085328983.html) | Iran’s foreign ministry publicly denied any nuclear-weapons role in doctrine, and Reuters noted that Khamenei has final authority over nuclear policy and had previously banned nuclear weapons in a fatwa. This is the strongest 2024 evidence that the official line was still restraint-oriented rather than openly reckless. | `1B.2` |
| `Iranian commander warns Tehran could review 'nuclear doctrine' amid Israeli threats` | Reuters | 2024-04-18 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/iranian-commander-warns-tehran-could-114201991.html) | A senior IRGC commander said Israeli threats could lead Tehran to review and deviate from its nuclear doctrine. That is direct brinkmanship language, even if it is framed as conditional deterrence rather than immediate use. | `1B.2` |
| `Iran to change nuclear doctrine if existence threatened, adviser to supreme leader says` | Reuters | 2024-05-09 | [link](https://www.dawn.com/news/1832474) | Kamal Kharrazi, an adviser to Khamenei, said Iran would change its nuclear doctrine if its existence were threatened and that there would be “no choice” but to alter military doctrine. This is among the clearest 2024 examples of nuclear brinkmanship in Khamenei’s orbit. | `1B.2` |
| `Supreme Leader Khamenei says Iran demonstrated its power against Israel` | Reuters | 2024-04-21 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/supreme-leader-khamenei-says-iran-demonstrated-its-power-against-israel/2050451/) | Khamenei thanked the armed forces for the April strike on Israel and described it as proof of Iran’s power. This is not nuclear rhetoric itself, but it reinforces a broader escalation posture rather than cautious de-escalatory messaging. | `1B.2` |

**Assessment**

- **Best-supported “responsible rhetoric” reading:** Khamenei’s system kept repeating the line that nuclear weapons were not part of Iran’s doctrine, and Reuters explicitly tied that to his ultimate authority.
- **Best-supported “irresponsible rhetoric” reading:** senior figures close to Khamenei used conditional threats about changing doctrine and moving away from prior considerations if Iran faced existential pressure.
- **Net judgment for 2024:** mixed, but leaning **not fully responsible**. The rhetoric was not openly apocalyptic or openly pro-nuclear-use, yet it included explicit doctrinal brinkmanship that falls short of careful restraint.

**Search gap**
- In this pass, I did **not** find a strong 2024 primary-source example of Khamenei personally using apocalyptic language, direct nuclear-use normalization, or a clearly reckless nuclear threat in his own voice.
- The evidence is mostly **indirect**: official doctrine denials on one side, and threats from commanders/advisers in his orbit on the other. That leaves 1B.2 partly inferential rather than cleanly established from Khamenei’s own words.
